# Python Scripting for Automation: requests, files, and libraries

## Overview
Now you turn Python into a real automation tool by connecting it to the outside world - APIs and files - which lets you build scripts that do genuine work. The requests library is the standard way to call APIs from Python: with a few lines you send a GET or POST, add headers (including your auth token), attach a JSON body, and read the JSON response straight into a dictionary you can process. This is the Python equivalent of the HTTP Request node, and it means any API you can reach in a no-code tool you can also reach in a script, with unlimited flexibility. You install libraries like requests using pip, Python's package manager, which opens access to thousands of ready-made tools. File handling is the other half: you will read and write plain text, CSV files (using the csv module or pandas for tabular data), and JSON files, so your scripts can process exports, generate reports, and hand data to other systems. A critical professional habit introduced here is keeping secrets out of your code by using environment variables (or a .env file) for API keys, rather than hard-coding them where they might leak. You will also get an overview of libraries that power automation - requests for HTTP, pandas for data, openpyxl for Excel, and others - so you know what to reach for. With API calls, file I/O, and safe secret handling, your Python scripts become capable standalone automations and powerful helpers inside n8n, exactly the low-code capability employers want alongside no-code fluency.

## Deep Dive
This module covers: Installing packages with pip; The requests library (GET/POST, headers, JSON); Reading/writing files, CSV, and JSON; Environment variables for secrets; Useful automation libraries overview. Mastering these ideas is essential because they appear repeatedly in production AI systems.

### What You Will Learn
- The core theory behind today's topic.
- How to apply it using Python, NumPy, Pandas, or the relevant framework.
- How to evaluate results and avoid common mistakes.
- Where to find authoritative references when you need deeper detail.

### Real-World Context
In industry, these skills are used daily: data scientists clean messy survey data, AI engineers deploy models to REST APIs, and automation engineers orchestrate pipelines. Today's practical task simulates one of these real-world scenarios.

## Hands-On Practice
Practical Task: Write a Python script that reads an API key from an environment variable, calls an API with requests, parses the JSON response, and writes selected fields to a CSV file.
Mini Project: Build a Python 'report generator': fetch data from an API, combine it with data read from a local CSV, transform it, and output both a cleaned CSV and a JSON summary - with the API key stored in an environment variable.
Assignment: Explain why secrets should be stored in environment variables rather than hard-coded, and show a before/after code snippet demonstrating the fix.

Complete all three sections. Each completed section earns points toward your CalibiAI Score. If you are unsure about any part, use the AI assessment popup to submit your work and receive dynamic feedback from DeepSeek.

## Common Mistakes to Avoid
Many beginners rush into coding before fully understanding the data. Others skip validation steps and overestimate model performance. This module helps you build the discipline of checking assumptions first, then applying algorithms systematically.

## Career Impact
The skills covered today are frequently tested in technical interviews and required in entry-level AI engineering roles. Building a portfolio that demonstrates mastery of these concepts will significantly improve your job prospects.

## Key Takeaways
1. Theory guides practice — understand before coding.
2. Clean data and clear metrics are more valuable than complex models.
3. Document your steps for reproducibility.
4. Communication matters: explain results to non-technical stakeholders.

## Next Steps After Today
